title: Kitchen English in Slow English 🍳 | Phrasal Verbs for Daily Life
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to a new episode
of Bow's Slow English. In today's
episode, you are going to learn some
phrasal verbs specifically relating to
the kitchen. I hope you learn a lot of
new vocabulary today. Before we get
started, please click like, subscribe,
and share this video with your friends.
And if you'd like to learn more phrasal
verbs, check out my ebooks. The link is
in the description below. A phrasal verb
is a verb plus a particle, which is a
small word like up, down, in, out, and
together it creates a new meaning. I
know phrasal verbs can be quite tricky
because there is so much to know. And
sometimes it is hard to figure out what
a phrasal verb means just from looking
at the word. So today, I'm going to show
you some examples so that you have a
visual and it will help you to
understand faster. I'm sure a lot of you
are wondering if I will ever cook again
in slow English. And I probably will
sometime soon. But for now, I'd love for
you to join me in my kitchen so we can
learn some new phrasal verbs. Come
follow me.
Also, I hope everyone is having a
beautiful day today or evening.
I am going to turn on the stove. First,
I will click the button in or the dial
in.
Then I will turn counterclockwise
to activate the gas.
Then I will turn the heat to high,
medium, or low.
So I just turned on the stove.
Now, let's turn off the stove by turning
the dial clockwise, which means to the
right. So this means clockwise.
This means counterclockwise.
I turned on the stove or I'm turning on
the stove, and I turned off the stove or
I'm turning off the stove. Next phrasal
verb is to heat up. I just grabbed some
bone broth from the refrigerator or the
fridge. I'll heat up the soup or I'll
heat up the bone broth. I'm pouring the
soup into the pot, and now I'll heat it
up.
You can also use the phrasal verb to
warm up. To heat up and to warm up mean
the same thing. The next phrasal verb we
will learn is to cut up or chop up.
I have an avocado and I have a cutting
board. I will use the knife to cut up or
chop up the avocado.
Here are a few phrasal verbs you can use
for eggs.
I am going to crack open the egg. And
after I've cracked open the egg,
I will mix it into the recipe.
I could also fry up the egg, which means
I will yet again crack open the egg into
a frying pan like this, and I will fry
up the egg. Another way to say mix in is
to stir in. This action is called
stirring. This is boil over.
Boil over means that you have a pot of
water and the heat is very high. The
water is boiling and bubbling so much
that it boils over. The next phrasal
verb is cook down. We will usually use
this phrasal verb when we talk about
making sauce. The sauce starts as a
liquid, then after it has been exposed
to some heat, it will cook down. So it
goes from a liquid to a thicker
consistency. And after the sauce has
been cooked down, we need it to cool
down, which means that we need to bring
the temperature down. Usually, that
means that you are setting it at room
temperature. If you like to bake bread,
there's a phrasal verb you could use
called bake off. So when you put the
bread in the oven, you can say I'm
baking off the bread.
Because I do not do much cooking or
baking, this isn't a phrasal verb that I
hear often or that I use often, but it's
certainly one that I've heard before.
And after I've finished cooking, I'm
going to serve up the dinner or I will
serve up the food. And all that means is
you are ready to give the food to your
loved ones to eat. Now, it's time for
clean up. So clean up means that you are
cleaning the kitchen. So you might wipe
down the counter, which is another
phrasal verb. You might put away the
groceries.
You might throw out the avocado peel.
I'm going to put the dirty dishes in the
dishwasher.
I will open up the dishwasher.
Let me know in the comments which
phrasal verbs were new to you, and did I
miss any? Can you think of any others
that are usable in the kitchen? I will
see you in the next video. Thank you so
much for watching, and I hope you share
this with your friends. Bye.
